reasoning: This was a Phase I dose-escalation safety study that successfully met its primary endpoint of determining dose-limiting toxicities. Step 1 (TARGET ENGAGEMENT): While direct target engagement evidence is limited, the NK cells were successfully infused at escalating doses with aldesleukin support, suggesting delivery to target tissues. Step 2 (PATHWAY MODULATION): The occurrence of GVHD and graft effects indicates the NK cells were biologically active and engaging with host tissues. Step 3 (CLINICAL TRANSLATION): The primary safety endpoint was met, with clear dose-toxicity relationships established across different donor types. Step 4 (POPULATION EFFECTS): Strong subgroup differences were observed - KIR mismatched haplo donors showed lower DLT rates at higher doses, while cord blood donors had higher DLT rates, particularly at the highest dose. This suggests donor source significantly impacts safety profile. Step 5 (CONFOUNDERS): No major confounders identified - appropriate Phase I design with adequate sample size (n=63) and follow-up duration.
